name: Domperidone
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Domperidone is cleared by the liver (CYP3A4), but its half-life almost triples in severe kidney impairment (7.4 to 20.8 hours at creatinine clearance [CrCl] below 30 mL/min/1.73 m2; single-dose plasma levels were lower than in healthy volunteers, so the reduction is for accumulation on repeated dosing). The European label reduces dosing to once or twice daily in severe impairment and may lower the dose. Its main risk is QT prolongation and sudden cardiac death, which electrolyte disturbances common in kidney failure make more likely. It has no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: SmPC section 5.2 defines severe renal impairment as creatinine clearance (CrCl) below 30 mL/min/1.73 m2.
chip: CrCl <30: once or twice daily only

bands.recommendation: Usual dose: 10 mg up to three times daily before meals; maximum 30 mg/day, usually for no more than 1 week (SmPC).
bands.short: Usual: 10 mg up to 3 times daily

bands.recommendation: No dose change specified (SmPC adjusts only in severe impairment). Keep to 30 mg/day maximum and the shortest course.
Severe impairment (CrCl <30): reduce dosing to once or twice daily depending on severity; the dose may also need reducing (SmPC).
Severe impairment: dose once or twice daily; consider a lower dose (SmPC). Check potassium, magnesium and QTc first.

hd.text: Dose as for severe impairment: once or twice daily, possibly a lower dose (SmPC). Dialysis removal not stated. Electrolyte shifts around dialysis raise QT risk; check QTc.
hd.short: Once or twice daily; watch QTc

pd.text: Dose as for severe impairment: once or twice daily, possibly a lower dose (SmPC). No PD data.

crrt.text: No data. Critically ill patients often have QT risk factors; avoid unless no alternative.

dialyzable: Not stated in the SmPC (91% to 93% protein-bound; removal unlikely to be meaningful).
monitoring: QTc and electrolytes (potassium, magnesium) before and during treatment in patients with kidney failure, heart disease or interacting drugs; stop if palpitations, syncope or arrhythmia symptoms. Contraindicated with QT-prolonging drugs and potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (SmPC 4.3, 4.4).

pediatric.approved_ages: Adolescents 12 years and older weighing 35 kg or more; efficacy not established under 12 years or under 35 kg (SmPC).
pediatric.usual_dose: 12 years and older, 35 kg or more: 10 mg up to three times daily; maximum 30 mg/day.

renal.recommendation: Adolescents 12 years and older (35 kg or more) follow adult kidney rules; not recommended in younger children.

adult: Severity grading in 4.2 is not numeric; 5.2 uses CrCl <30 mL/min/1.73 m2, which we use as the threshold for 'severe'.
Dialyzability: SmPC silent; the dialyzable line is our inference from protein binding (flag).
